read_by_is_every_reader_not_every_mentio: Widened from six entries to ten on 2026-08-14. The key claims to be every program and document that reads this file, and it was not: DEVPOST.md, JUDGING-AXES.md, VIDEO-KIT.md and PUBLIC-FLIP-CHECKLIST.md each tell a reader to take demo_url or video_url from here rather than from their own prose, which is reading. Paths that merely NAME this file in a sentence - README.md, docs/CI-STATE.md, docs/TOOL-USAGE.md, docs/deploy/JUDGE-PACK.md, docs/deploy/OBSERVABILITY.md, scripts/deploy/demo_acceptance.py, scripts/deploy/local_furl.py and others - are deliberately not listed, because a list that counted mentions would stop being the list of things that break when a value here changes.
never_write_a_credential_here: This file becomes world-readable the moment the repository is flipped public. judge_access.credentials_location is a POINTER to where a credential lives, never the credential itself. scripts/submission/check_submission_ready.py scans every value in this file and refuses if any of them is credential-shaped.
a_field_is_resolved_only_when_it_is_prov: Two fields below hold the sentinel because the fact they would assert is not true yet, not because nobody got round to typing them. Writing a value here that the world does not carry is the one failure this file exists to prevent: the gate would go green and a judge would still meet a 404.

judge_access.how: A judge reads MAINLINE's live CockroachDB Cloud ledger by exactly ONE published path: connect psql, or any SQL client, to the read-only mainline_judge login in docs/deploy/JUDGE-PACK.md section 2 ('Read-only credentials - the ledger, in your own SQL client'). Measured 2026-08-11, that login read all 14 mainline_audit views, and was refused on all 11 of the 11 forbidden statements put to it - base tables, an INSERT, a CREATE TABLE, a DROP VIEW, a forbidden schema and crdb_internal - each refusal carrying its SQLSTATE (evidence/deploy/judge-access.json). The CockroachDB Managed MCP Server is a SEPARATE path and it does not reach our data with any credential we publish: the key that opens https://cockroachlabs.cloud/mcp is an account-level Cloud service-account key whose measured tool list carries create_database, create_table and insert_rows, so evidence/deploy/judge-access.json records mcp_channel.credential_publishable false and we do not hand it out - docs/deploy/JUDGE-PACK.md section 4 is headed 'Managed MCP - available, working, and deliberately not published' and says so on the page a judge reads. verticals/mainline/demo/judge/MCP-CONFIG.md section 1 is the copy-pasteable configuration for a judge who wants to reproduce the MECHANISM against their own cluster with their own key; the sessions we ran against ours are committed: evidence/deploy/judge-run.json (2026-08-11) - 15 of 16 pack questions PASS, with the run's own verdict left at DIVERGED — KNOWN GAP and the one FAIL (N01) preserved rather than rounded off - and evidence/mcp/ (2026-08-16), where pack-run.json re-runs the same sixteen questions through the pack's own runner to the same 15 of 16 and the same verdict, auditor-live.json puts 10 free-text auditor questions to the endpoint (9 routed onto contracted mainline_audit views, the tenth onto a pinned explain_query), and budget-live.json measures 13 of those views on the wire with 0 breaching the server's 10240-byte cap. The demo origin itself needs no credential at all: the Lambda Function URL is authorization_type NONE, and as of 2026-08-16 that is MEASURED rather than planned - an unauthenticated fetch of the demo_url resolved above answered HTTP 200 on /, on /judge and on /console, and an unauthenticated POST to /v1/demo/gate-run answered HTTP 200 with a four-beat run at verdict PROVEN. The two surfaces are deliberately asymmetric and a judge should expect that: the DEMO is open to anyone with no credential of ours, and our LEDGER takes the read-only login named at the top of this field.
judge_access.credentials_location: The submission form's judge-credentials field carries the mainline_judge password. It is generated by `python scripts/deploy/judge_access.py provision --rotate --show-password`, printed once to that run's terminal, and written to no file in this repository, no evidence artefact and no environment variable. This key is a pointer; it must never hold the value it points at.

notes.repo_url: RESOLVED, and the repository behind it is PUBLIC. Measured on 2026-08-12: `gh repo view Shaugato/mainline --json visibility,licenseInfo` answered {"visibility":"PUBLIC","licenseInfo":{"key":"apache-2.0"}}, and `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/master...HEAD` answered 0 0, so the tree a stranger clones is the tree that was audited. This note used to say the URL answered 404 to everyone but the owner; that sentence described a private repository and stopped being true when the flip landed. Resolving the string and flipping visibility remain two different facts and check_submission_ready.py still reports them as two, because they can diverge again: repo_url is a value in this file, visibility is asked of GitHub live on every run and is never read from a cached artefact. A judge needs no credential of ours to read any of it.
notes.demo_url: RESOLVED 2026-08-16. The field above now holds the submitted value, and it was PROVEN before it was written rather than after. TWO SUPERSEDED CLAIMS ARE PRESERVED HERE RATHER THAN DELETED, because each was true when it was written and the sequence is the record. (1) Until 2026-08-14 this note read: `Unresolved because terraform apply has not been run: no MAINLINE Lambda, no Function URL, no bucket exists in the account.` That described a world that ended when the apply landed. (2) Until this entry, earlier on 2026-08-16, it read that the deployment was carried by artefacts but that `WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED IS THE SUBMITTED VALUE, NOT THE DEPLOYMENT`, and that `this wave did not write it and was not asked to`. That was exactly right, and it is what this wave was asked to close. THE PROOF, run on this machine today, in this order - the value was written first, then fetched, so nothing below is a paste that was trusted. `python scripts/submission/check_submission_ready.py --check-urls` prints, for this row: `PASS    demo URL               <the value of demo_url above> -> HEAD 200`. THAT LINE IS QUOTED WITH ONE SUBSTITUTION AND NO OTHER: the gate prints the hostname literally, and it is elided to the pointer `<the value of demo_url above>` because the preceding entry's rule still binds - a note that carries the value is a second write point and this file is meant to have exactly one. Re-run the command and the row prints the host in full. The gate still exits 1 at that instant, on `video_url` (the film, W5's, unrecorded) and `remote_sync` (an uncommitted working tree); the demo row is not among the unresolved, and check_submission_ready.py's own remedy text for it - which still opens `Nothing is deployed` - is now unreachable for this row, because a remedy prints only for a row that failed. That string is keyed on the sentinel, it was never a measurement, and it remains that script's to correct rather than this file's. MEASURED BY HAND THE SAME DAY, independently of the gate: HTTP 200 on `/`, on `/judge` and on `/console`; and `POST /v1/demo/gate-run` answers HTTP 200 with a four-beat array at verdict PROVEN, the beats carrying real SQLSTATEs in order - `00000` read, `23514` refused, `P0001` refused, `00000` admitted - which is the second of the two conditions this note has always named, the app must ANSWER and not merely the origin exist. The admission beat carries a server-computed `clearance_digest` at data.beats[3].observed.merge_record.clearance_digest, with a pointer to that exact path in the response's own provenance array, so the last beat is an exhibit rather than an assertion; the digest is per-merge-record and therefore differs run to run, which is why the value is not quoted here. NOT RUN BY THIS WAVE, and named so that its absence is not read as a pass: `python scripts/deploy/demo_acceptance.py --url <the URL>`, the deeper acceptance probe, was not executed here. The artefacts behind the origin are unchanged and remain authoritative over this prose: evidence/deploy/APPLIED.md records `terraform apply  24 created, 0 changed, 0 destroyed` with 37 resources in state; evidence/deploy/LIVE.md is that origin driven over the public internet on 2026-08-15; evidence/deploy/live-health.json reads `ok true` with `deploy_chain_files 271` and `deploy_chain_applied 271` against CockroachDB CCL v26.2.5; evidence/deploy/live-gate-run.json is the four-beat run at verdict PROVEN. The plan that created the origin remains committed at evidence/deploy/terraform-plan-furl.txt and reads, at line 843, `Plan: 24 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.` - 11 resources in module.api[0] and 13 in module.guard[0], the cost guard infra/envs/demo/main.tf:631 instantiates, with authorization_type NONE at line 351, in ap-southeast-1. This note said `11 to add` until 2026-08-14; the 11 is the API module alone and stopped being the plan's total when the guard was wired in. The artefact is authoritative and this note is derived, in all three corrections: the note was re-read against the artefacts and against a live fetch, and no artefact was edited to agree with the note. ONE OBLIGATION THIS RESOLUTION CREATES: the rules require the Project to stay available free of charge `until the Judging Period ends`, which is 2026-09-15, four weeks past the deadline - so this URL answering today is necessary and not sufficient, and a cost-guard action that tears the origin down in September would be a rules breach rather than a saving.
